title: Manual QA Report — Ancillaries & Seat Map (Air Cairo NDC)

fields.label: Scope
fields.value: Supplier Feature Ancillaries -> Supplier Air Cairo NDC (air-sm-cairo), Portal, 100 executable-scope cases of a 126-case sheet

fields.label: Coverage
fields.value: 100 cases executed (72 Passed, 7 Failed, 2 Blocked, 1 Skipped, 13 Not Executed, 5 N/A).

fields.label: Description
fields.value: Manual Execution of the Ancillaries suite against Air Cairo staging Portal; a real Hold-then-Pay booking and a real Confirmed booking were completed; two supplier-enforced negative rules were proven by real Hold/Book rejection.

summary.title: 1. Executive Summary
summary.totalLabel: Total Suite Cases (100 executable this run)

cases.title: Closed passenger sections still report missing information

rows.label: Notes
rows.value: Multiple sub-checks failed: a collapsed passenger section's First Name field remained genuinely editable; two accordion sections could be open simultaneously; and an incomplete-but-collapsed passenger blocked Next with no visible signal on the collapsed header (no badge/error count) - only correct behaviour was that Next itself is blocked and Expand All resurfaces the Required markers.

cases.title: The rule is rechecked when you switch passenger

rows.label: Notes
rows.value: Distinct from EXR-002/003 (whether the rule is enforced at all): this case is specifically about whether the seat map's displayed state changes per passenger/per infant-assignment. It was directly and conclusively observed to never change (identical aria-label regardless of which passenger or infant-assignment is active) - a UI defect finding, not a re-statement of EXR-002/003.

cases.title: The rule follows the infant's linked adult

rows.label: Notes
rows.value: Same UI-defect finding as EXR-004: switching the infant's Assigned to between adults changed nothing about the seat's displayed state or availability.

cases.title: Three journeys give three seat maps and three sets of ancillaries

rows.label: Notes
rows.value: Partly Passed, partly Failed on a 2-leg multi-city itinerary: seat maps and meal panels were correctly split one-per-flight, but the Extra Baggage panel existed only for the outbound leg and was entirely absent for the return leg - the same underlying journey-scoping defect as TC-SM-MCT-006.

cases.title: Extra baggage should say which flight it belongs to

rows.label: Notes
rows.value: On the 2-leg multi-city trip, only one Extra Baggage panel exists (headed for the outbound leg); the return leg's baggage options are not offered anywhere. Confirms the sheet's own known-fault class (baggage not correctly scoped per journey), though the exact shape (missing panel vs merged/mislabelled panel) differs from the sheet's original description.

cases.title: Seat and ancillary charges should be identifiable per journey

rows.label: Notes
rows.value: Reproduces the sheet's own known fault exactly: with one seat on each of two separate flights, the Fare Breakdown showed one merged base-fare line, one merged tax line and one merged Seat Selection total (614+236=850) - none itemised per journey.

cases.title: Going back a step must not silently throw away seats and ancillaries

rows.label: Notes
rows.value: Confirmed defect (cross-supplier, first found on flynas in run-006): editing a passenger's First Name after choosing ancillaries silently discarded the held seat and its EGP 1,180 fare line, with no warning, toast or dialog. High/P1 - see Defect Register.

cases.title: A seat booked on one flight never appears against another

rows.label: Notes
rows.value: Submitting Hold on the 2-leg multi-city itinerary failed with a browser-level CORS error on the fare-recheck-hold call, before the page ever navigated away from Passenger Info. The precondition (a completed Hold/Book to inspect) could not be reached at all - recorded Blocked by this technical error, not scored Pass/Fail. Raised separately as its own technical finding, not folded into the case verdict.

cases.title: Seats and ancillaries survive to the confirmation page per flight

rows.label: Notes
rows.value: Same CORS blocker as TC-SM-MCT-004 - the Hold needed to reach the confirmation/e-ticket page never completed. Not scored Pass/Fail.

categories.name: N/A — Structural (not applicable on this supplier)

cases.title: You cannot reach the seats without choosing a fare package

rows.label: Notes
rows.value: Air Cairo has no in-wizard bundle step at all (fare package is chosen at search, before Passenger Info) - there is nothing for this case to gate on. Not scored as a failure.

cases.title: Missing passenger details and a missing fare package are both reported

rows.label: Notes
rows.value: Compound case: the missing-passenger-details half was directly confirmed reported (8 Required markers). The missing-fare-package half cannot occur on this supplier (no such wizard step, same structural reason as TC-SM-NAV-002), so the case as a whole is recorded N/A - final, most-informed verdict supersedes the earlier partial Passed reading.

cases.title: Infants appear as passengers but carry no seat or ancillaries

rows.label: Notes
rows.value: This particular order has no infant (1 adult only), so the counting behaviour could not be checked on it directly; already covered on the separate 4-passenger booking earlier in this run, where the infant correctly had zero ancillary sections (TC-SM-PAX-001).

cases.title: Extra baggage must not clash with the baggage already in the fare package

rows.label: Notes
rows.value: Air Cairo's baggage model has no discrete weight tiers (only per-kilogram/equipment items), so the exact same-weight clash this case requires cannot be constructed - already established under TC-BG-003. Not scored as a failure; flagged for test design to generalise the wording.

cases.title: Seat map and ancillary prices use the right exchange rate

rows.label: Notes
rows.value: Air Cairo prices natively in EGP with no currency conversion at any point, so there is no Rate-Of-Exchange division for this case to check. Not scored as a failure.

cases.title: A taken seat can be looked at but not booked

rows.label: Notes
rows.value: Recorded Not Executed as written in the results doc: on this supplier a genuinely sold seat is removed from the map entirely rather than shown disabled/viewable, so the case's own precondition (taken-but-still-viewable) never occurs on this supplier's data model. Not a defect - a different, internally consistent design choice.

cases.title: A changed price is shown before the booking screen

rows.label: Notes
rows.value: Price-mismatch trigger (fareMismatch true) could not be reproduced on Air Cairo across four separate searches/dates/fare classes; every decoded flight-token carried fareMismatch false. Not a defect - data/supplier-driven precondition never occurred this session.

items.body: Editing a passenger's First Name after choosing ancillaries silently discards the held seat and its fare line — no warning, toast or dialog is shown. Now confirmed on two suppliers (flynas in run-006, Air Cairo here), on two currencies, two ancillary models and two environments — a Feature-level defect in the booking wizard, not a supplier integration problem.
items.evidence: Seat summary and fare total before/after the name edit, quoted in ManualExecutionResults.md; empty alert/toast containers recorded at the moment of loss.

items.body: Closed passenger sections fail three of four expected behaviours: a collapsed section's field remains genuinely editable; two accordion sections can be open simultaneously; and an incomplete, collapsed passenger blocks Next with no visible signal on its own header (no badge, no error count) — only manual expansion reveals which passenger is the problem.

The exit-row/infant-restriction seat's displayed state (aria-label, availability) never changes regardless of which passenger is active or which adult the infant is assigned to — byte-identical output across every passenger tried. The underlying rule IS enforced by the supplier at Hold/Book (see TC-SM-EXR-002/003, both Passed), but the seat map itself gives the agent no warning before submitting.

fields.label: Reproducibility
fields.value: Always, on every passenger/assignment switch tried

items.body: A 2-leg multi-city booking gets only one Extra Baggage panel (for the outbound leg); the return leg has no baggage panel or options offered at all. Seat maps and meal panels are correctly split one-per-flight on the same booking.

Seat and ancillary charges across two separate flights on one itinerary are shown as one merged base-fare line, one merged tax line and one merged Seat Selection total, not itemised per journey — reproduces the test sheet's own known-fault description exactly on a different supplier.

Submitting Hold on a 2-leg multi-city itinerary fails outright with a browser-level CORS error on the 'fare-recheck-hold' call — the request never reaches the server in a way the browser accepts, and the page never leaves Passenger Info. A single-flight Hold never hits this error in this run. Needs a developer, not a retest.

A calcBaggagePrice null-dereference console error (Cannot read properties of null, reading 'baggageMetaData') fires on every baggage change. First seen on flynas in run-006 under a completely different baggage data model and environment; now reproduces identically on Air Cairo. The computed price is still correct in both cases — not scored against any case, but worth a developer's eye as a latent defect in a pricing code path.

sections.title: Assumptions & Risks Resolved
blocks: TC-SM-PAX-008 (two infant-holding adults, one seat set): an initial UI-only reading and a first real Book attempt were inconclusive/confounded by an unrelated invalid document number. Two clean retries (Book and Hold, confound removed) were consistently rejected by the supplier — the rule is real and enforced at order submission, not in the seat map.

TC-SM-EXR-002/003 (exit-row restriction): resolved from an initial UI-only Failed reading to Passed once real Hold attempts were genuinely and specifically rejected by the supplier ("SPECIFIC SEAT REQUESTED NOT AVAILABLE - RESTRICTED"). The UI-only reading described what the seat map offers, not what the supplier accepts.

TC-SM-EXR-004/005 remain Failed — a separate question (does the seat map's own displayed state change per passenger) with its own direct, repeated evidence that it does not, independent of whether the underlying rule holds elsewhere (it does).
TC-SM-CNF-018 and the calcBaggagePrice console error are now each confirmed on two suppliers, raising both to Feature-level findings.

An early meal-price observation (a 20.00 EGP decline cost, and no free-meal option) was explicitly WITHDRAWN after a DOM-parsing mistake was identified and corrected with a screenshot; the real value is SRV42 at 0.00 EGP, and a free decline option genuinely exists.
A new confirmed Supplier Rule: Air Cairo Document Number must be a capital A followed by 8 digits, recorded via module_manager/cli.js supplier-feature supplier rules.

sections.title: Known Limitations
blocks: Portal only — no Admin-app pass has been run against Air Cairo.
